title: 🧭 Eryndor Living Atlas III — Tharvorn, Sahrad, Orundel & Vaelora
rawNotionMarkup: Original new travel-world expansion — all four continents beyond Avarra. Existing continent names, macro environments, races, supernatural limits, and ancient mystery guardrails are preserved. Every newly named state, city, village, polity, river reach, trade guild and route below is new proposed/created material for the Year 3,847 living atlas. Figures are approximate Year 3,847 modeled residents, not an exact census. The world does not move until gameplay advances; mere documentation does not mean Gloin knows these places. ## Cultural gazetteers and living local identities ## Regional cultures and subcultures — new complete living-culture expansion Explicit creator rule: Every intelligent people has multiple cultures; every region contains overlapping local subcultures. The distinctive Khazari idea that contribution earns respect is not a generic value imposed on Eldar, Urakai, Halflings, Centaurs, Merfolk, Goblins or other peoples. Each community has its own admired paths, kinship traditions, duties, taboos and dissenting individuals. Culture comes from species + continent + settlement + state + occupation + household + life experience, and shared multi-species village identity can override older labels. 1. Eryndor Living Culture Atlas VIII — Thrones, Eldar, Urakai, Humans & Elder Courts: Seven independent Khazari traditions, multiple Eldar/Urakai branches, five human power-group subcultures, Drakari and Aelwyn courts. 2. Eryndor Living Culture Atlas IX — Smaller Peoples & Regional Traditions: Halflings, Gnomes, Goblins, Ents, Centaurs, Merfolk, Giants, the nine later-established peoples, and guarded unknowns for Living Mountains. 3. Eryndor Living Culture Atlas X — Animal Peoples, Diasporas & Mixed Communities: Wolvenkin, Foxfolk, Lionfolk, Tigerfolk, Elephantfolk, Bearfolk, Cowfolk and Pigfolk, all with several regional alternatives. 4. Eryndor Living Culture Atlas XI — All Peoples by Continent & Regional Subcultures: 28 modeled peoples × 5 continents regional crosswalk, 28 distinct cultural zones among five continents, shared mixed-town and professional subcultures, and methods for generating persistent local variation. Authority: These are new, creator-revisable setting expansions, not recovered original history or dialogue. Old confirmed ethnic/political foundations and Gloin's story take priority. No birth rates, marriage ratios, offspring biology, family sizes, lifespans or population totals change. Big families and centuries-long craft pursuits coexist, and no NPC gains world knowledge automatically. Current in-game time remains Autumn Day 22, Year 3,847, 11:25 AM. ## Sixfold world census is now the current baseline — 21 November 2026 Population resimulation completed: The creator explicitly accepted a 6× revision of previously simulated Year 3847 populations. The current modeled world total is 2,062.800 million residents (formerly 343.800m), with Avarra 1,019.760m, Tharvorn 171.000m, Sahrad 282.222m, Orundel 393.600m and Vaelora 196.218m. The 28-people by five-continent matrix, 133 previously quantified named settlement/Throne entries, the 18 resident categories of Bramblebridge, and the 8 other quantified patchwork places, plus habitat and carrying-capacity constraints, are audited in Eryndor Living Census XII — Sixfold Population & Carrying-Capacity Audit. Priority and supersession: All old 343.8m, 24m Khazari, 22m Seven Thrones, 18m Eldar, 31m Urakai and 3.8m Karak-Varn figures in the preserved legacy text are superseded as current demographic estimates by 6× figures. They remain intact only as historical reference or original simulation baselines. New: 144m global Khazari; 132m Seven-Throne domain subtotal included in the 144m; 22.8m Karak-Varn included in the Thrones. Do NOT add these overlapping totals. Long-lived peoples retain unchanged birth rates, and any specific community may still face housing, food, water and supply crises because the new populations are not equally concentrated. This is a historical-scale editorial resimulation, not 6× births during the current play session. No old ancient First Throne uncertain peak estimate or unnamed uncensused species is automatically multiplied. Gloin's Year 3847, Era of Crowns, Fifth Age campaign remains paused at Hadrik's desk, Autumn Day 22 \~11:25 AM. ## Planetary population redesign applies to all continents — creator direction The 50,000-km Twin Titans world is expected to contain much more rural population, scattered villages and small regional cities, with its old capitals greatly expanded in long-established inhabited cores. The creator emphasized Avarra “and the likes,” so Tharvorn, Sahrad, Orundel and Vaelora are also candidates for analogous regionally differentiated enlargement rather than being left as tiny afterthoughts. Old city, continent and worldwide population counts are model baselines pending review, not current newly locked numbers. Preserve some isolated wilderness, cultural distinctions, ordinary demographic behaviour and all established birth rates; see Eryndor Living Atlas I — Continents, Habitats & Population Model for the full demographic revision policy. No exact multiplier, count, city rename, migration event or story progress is fixed here. ## Crossing the world: sea distances are not shortcuts - The Northern Ocean and Stormward Sea divide northern Avarra from Tharvorn. Routes sail with coastal pilots, late-season storms and ice closures. Not every northern port runs a regular service. - The Crown Sea and Sapphire Strait connect southern Avarra with Sahrad. Merchants ship grain, spice, dyes, wool, animals, ceramics and machinery; port duties, naval escorts and seasonal winds decide actual costs. - The Eastern Ocean separates Avarra from Orundel, with ocean passages from eastern river ports and island stages. The western Orundel coast is not one government. - The Western Ocean separates Avarra's merchant shore from Vaelora. Long crossings carry insurance, water, cargo manifests and storm risk; Merfolk polities have their own sovereign marine routes. - Sail plan at 100–200 km/day in viable conditions per established Geography; do not guarantee passage length without a named route, season, wind and docking plans. Rare magitech transport is not ordinary economy travel. ## Tharvorn — frost forests, the Worldbreak and southern fjords Modeled residents: 28.5m, consisting of 15m humans, 2m Urakai, 1.6m Goblins, 1.1m Bearfolk, 1m Merfolk in adjacent shelves, 0.9m Centaurs, 0.7m Eldar, 0.7m Wolvenkin, 0.5m Khazari diaspora and others. Inhabited southern fjords and wind-sheltered valleys coexist with vast empty ice fields. Regional model: Southern fjords and farmland 10.8m; central conifer woods 6.2m; interior Northern Steppe 7.1m; remote alpine/glacial settlements 4.4m. A single Tharvorn empire does not exist; river-city leagues, independent north chiefs, inland clan routes and coastal agreements overlap. ### Named Tharvorn destinations | Place | Geographic position; A reported Living Mountain site cannot be promoted from giant folklore to fact without discovery. ## Exiled dark mages — complete political and social isolation from outsiders (creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON — NO OUTSIDE RELATIONS: From their formation by outcast magical practitioners at the beginning of the Era of Fire, and during their established survival well into the Third Age, the dark-mage groups of the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes did not develop relations with anyone outside their own group. They established no diplomatic relations, trade ties, alliances, treaties or cooperative political relationships with neighboring peoples, polities or communities. Treat them as an isolated power that remained apart from other societies, not a regular participant in interregional commerce, diplomacy or political coalitions. Their internal organization, personal associations among exiles, and succession across generations remain open; this does not mean they had no community among themselves. Precision: This is a correction to earlier speculative language about the mages “developing relationships with surrounding peoples.” Such external relationships did not happen. Historical encounters, threats, conflicts or observations from outsiders are not automatically established or precluded by this statement; do not invent such events. Their knowledge, exact longevity, later fate, and whether their tradition survives to the Fifth Age remain unresolved. Do not attribute dark-mage deeds to all Urakai or other inhabitants of the larger southeastern badlands region. ## Era of Fire's ending — the mages harnessed the volcano and unknowingly grew in power (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CANON EVENT AT SECOND AGE → THIRD AGE: The exiled dark mages had created the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano through dark magic at the beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322). At the end of that era (Year 1,437), planetwide earthquakes, whose aftershocks were amplified tenfold across the globe by the ancient Ironspine mountain ring, intensified their magically created volcano. The mages harnessed the power of the volcano itself to keep it from erupting with the full potential destructive force it otherwise could have had. Their intervention reduced the severity of the volcanic catastrophe; it does not establish that there was no eruption at all, no damage, or no casualties. Unforeseen effect: In channeling and restraining that volcanic power, the dark mages unknowingly acquired even greater magical power themselves. This increase in their power is an established consequence of the containment effort, although they did not know or understand it at the time. The exact metaphysical mechanism, quantitative strength increase, whether every mage gained equally, and the time and manner of any later recognition remain unknown. Their continued presence well into the Third Age is established independently; the power gain is not automatically proved to be the sole reason they survived the worldwide disaster. Continuity: The volcano was created by dark magic at the start of the Era of Fire, and was intensified by global earthquakes at the end; the mages then contained some of its destructive power, inadvertently augmenting themselves. None of this constitutes friendly diplomacy, outside alliances or trade; the dark mages remained socially and politically isolated. The origins and exact identity of their dark magical source, the exact technique for harnessing a volcanic force, and their later Third Age history remain open. Nor is a connection to the First Throne or to the separately undefined species-survival magical force established. ## Dark-mage continuity — endured well into the Third Age (creator canon, 21 November 2026) NEW CHRONOLOGICAL FACT: The dark-mage groups exiled from their villages at the beginning of the 116-year Era of Fire, who banded together in the formerly fertile southeastern agricultural lands of Avarra and deliberately created the Southern Wastes and their volcano with dark magic, were NOT confined to the Second Age. These dark-mage groups, their communities and practice continued WELL INTO THE THIRD AGE. The global earthquakes at the end of the Second Age (Second Age Year 1,437) therefore did NOT end their existence as a continuing dark-mage presence. The volcano they had created early in the Era of Fire was also intensified by the ending earthquakes; creation and later intensification are distinct events. Do not overdefine the survival: “Lasted well into the Third Age” is an intentionally broad period, not a fixed number of years or confirmation that each individual founder survived that long. The continuance may encompass successive generations, settlements, groups or traditions; the precise institutions and continuity of named founders are unwritten. Do not assign exact Third Age dates, sovereigns, wars, bloodlines, defeats, religion, expanded borders, extinction, destruction, migration, or a confirmed Fifth Age continuation. Neither their disappearance nor their survival to the present has been established. Dark magic is not attributed to an entire race, and the southern Urakai civilizations cannot be cast as the perpetrators by species. Protected chronology: (1) Second Age Year 1,322 — dark-mage exiles unite, magically transform southeastern Avarran fertile farmland into the Southern Wastes and create its volcano; (2) Second Age Year 1,437 — planetwide earthquakes shake the world, amplified tenfold globally by ancient Ironspine and intensifying the previously created volcano, ending Second Age and beginning Third Age; (3) a significant but UNNUMBERED span well into the Third Age — the dark mages endure. How they survived the natural catastrophe or interacted with the separately established yet-unidentified magical force involved in preventing species extinction is not known. First Throne involvement is an open, noncanon story option; Gloin's ancestry is unchanged and unresolved. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime in the Third Age, intending first to besiege the dwarven Khazari strongholds and then to attack Eldar and human kingdoms. Their exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, first Orc communities, degree of subsequent mage control and actual military results remain UNDECIDED. No Orc inhabitants, settlements, armies or history can occur in the Second Age's Awakening (Years 1–321), Wonder (Years 322–1,321) or Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), or the First Age. Earlier lore placing Orcs there is superseded and noncanon. Goblins and Ogres may predate the Third Age. Ambition does not prove these sieges or attacks were carried out; later Orc peoples have distinct cultures, agency and moral variation. CREATOR CANON — Orc creation by the Southern Wastes dark mages: The dark mages created the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and their volcano in the Second Age's Era of Fire, restrained its quake-amplified power at that Age's end (unknowingly strengthening themselves), then survived into the Third Age. During the Third Age they created the Orcs by an as-yet-undecided method, to advance their ambition to besiege Khazari strongholds first and eventually attack Eldar and human kingdoms. The intention and creator–creation relationship are now settled; exact date, process, locations, numbers, later power structure and whether specific attacks succeeded or even took place are not. The mages' isolation means no established diplomatic alliances, trade or treaties with previously existing outside peoples, not that they never created a new people. Modern Urakai are not collectively evil or automatically controlled by the ancient mages. Effects on war histories: Any established older east–west wars involving Urakai, and any historical Goblin/Ogre alliances or assistance with Orc forces, must have happened in the Third Age or later, with no specific Age within that range, reign, battle, migration date or formal state assigned yet. The anti-Goblin, anti-Ogre and anti-Urakai prejudices of western Avarra remain valid consequences of those undated wars. These cannot predate the Third Age. Nor should living Urakai's settled southeast badlands homelands and their modern peoples/cultures be erased or treated as magically evil due to a speculative ancient link. Canon controls and campaign: Modern Urakai exist in large numbers, with sophisticated diverse societies, independent cities, families, economies, politics, culture and varied morality. Existing Fifth Age maps and sixfold census are unchanged; this corrects only their ancestral chronology. No changes to family rates, species lifespans or present demographics. The no-species-extinction rule at the Second Age-ending earthquake stays: Urakai were not a species that survived that disaster, because they had not appeared yet; all peoples existing at that time survived somewhere. Do not connect their origin to Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unknown genealogy, the First Throne, the lost First Age moon-magics or the yet-unexplained global species-survival magical force without an explicit new creator decision. ## Era of Fire — exile of dark mages and magical creation of the Southern Wastes (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CREATOR-ESTABLISHED FOUNDING EVENT, NOT A PROPOSAL: At the very beginning of the Era of Fire, the third and final era of Eryndor's 1,437-year Second Age (beginning in Second Age Year 1,322), certain groups of mages found a way to practice newly accessed dark magic. They were cast out of their home villages because of their discovery or practice. The scattered exiles banded together in the southern lands. Those lands were NOT originally wastes: they had been fertile farming country with established agricultural communities. Deliberate transformation: At the outset of the Era of Fire, the united dark mages used their new-found dark magic to transform that fertile farmland into the bleak Southern Wastes, deliberately turning productive lands into a wasteland that became their own home. The devastation is an act of the exiled mage groups, not a natural original desert, not a consequence to be misassigned to the planetwide earthquakes at the END of the Era of Fire, and not a landform that had always been infertile. These are two separate established events at opposite ends of the 116-year era. Geographical identity — CREATOR NOW FIXED: “the Southern Wastes” created by the exiled dark mages are located on AVARRA, in the SOUTHEASTERN PART OF THE CREATOR'S APPROVED CONTINENT MAP, in the portion MARKED WITH A VOLCANO. This is NOT Sahrad and must NOT be merged with Sahrad's independently established Red Wastes, Glass Desert, or Sunscorched Expanse. This confirms that the formerly fertile farming country destroyed by the exiled mages at the opening of the Era of Fire occupies part of the southeastern volcanic/badlands region of Avarra. TWO-STAGE VOLCANO HISTORY — CREATOR CORRECTION: The volcano was CREATED by the exiled mages' DARK MAGIC at the very beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322), when they deliberately transformed fertile southeastern Avarran farmland into their Southern Wastes home. It did NOT exist before the dark-mage transformation and was not originally created by the earthquakes. However, at the END of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,437), the planetwide earthquakes and globally tenfold-amplified aftershocks intensified the ALREADY-EXISTING MAGICAL VOLCANO. Both events shaped its present state: magical creation first, seismic intensification later. The exact volcanic response (eruption frequency, magnitude, lava fields, ash, secondary effects), whether the first magical creation involved an eruption, and particular local casualties remain unspecified. Do not erase either the original dark-magic cause or the later earthquake-driven intensification, and do not automatically attribute the entire Southern Wastes' creation to the age-ending earthquake. Exact boundaries and the specific volcano's proper name have not been supplied; don't assume every southeastern badland, every volcanic zone, or all current Urakai territory was magically transformed. Respect the many established permanent Urakai, Goblin, Ogre, Kobold, Gnome and other communities of modern southeastern Avarra; do not make Urakai responsible for the mages' act by ethnicity or geography. Their urban and pastoral communities may survive among safe valleys, wells and habitable zones in the wider southeastern region. The modern sixfold census is not changed, nor are the names or locations of any existing settlements automatically reassigned. Magic and moral distinction: Eryndor already has intrinsically good, morally grey and intrinsically evil magics. This event confirms that these mage groups gained access to and used dark magic; it does NOT yet name a source moon, deity, magical discipline, patron, spell, ritual, unique innovation or specify whether that power itself was newly born at this moment rather than newly discovered/learned by the mages. Do not equate every mage, magic user, people or regional inhabitant with these exiles. Nor is the “fire” in the Era of Fire's name yet explicitly explained by this incident alone, unless the creator decides that. Unsettled details — do not fill automatically: Exact races and numbers of mages, identities and motivations of their villages, original names and states of the farming communities, how rapidly the land transformed, what happened to the farmers, whether any groups opposed the exiles, the detailed Third Age history of their enduring settlements and magical lineage (the groups are now established as surviving well into the Third Age, but their ultimate fate remains open), and whether the dark magic connects to the First Throne or later global earthquakes are all OPEN. Do not assert an extinct species or apply modern census values to ancient populations. The creator earlier restricted free-form invention in the third era, but has now directly authorized this specific event. This historical restriction was later superseded: the creator authorized detailed Era of Fire cultures, kingdoms, rulers and wars, which are now recorded in the Era of Fire chronicle and Second Age Annals. Do not invent an unapproved additional globe-wide catastrophe, a First Throne role, or specific dark-mage encounters. Era boundary protections: The Era of Fire lasted 116 years (Years 1,322–1,437). Its ending global earthquakes reached the vastly older-than-First-Age Ironspine ring, whose central position and deep roots magnified their aftershocks tenfold across Eryndor; sudden lowland and marshland uplift (including far-western Avarran mountain creation) caused immense deaths but no species extinctions, with some protective contribution by a yet undefined magical force. The beginning dark-mage terraforming has NO established causal link to the ending earthquakes or extinction-prevention magic. The First Throne connection remains a speculative possibility, and Gloin's unknown ancestry and paused campaign are not changed. ## Sahrad — desert mathematics, fertile rivers and the southern sultanates Modeled residents: 47.037m. Humans 30m, Merfolk 2.8m, Lionfolk 1.6m, Elephantfolk 1.65m, Urakai 1.3m, Goblins 1.1m, Kobolds 0.7m, and numerous smaller communities. Vast open desert has almost no inhabitants; dense river and oasis corridors account for much of the population. Regional model: Sahradi river-and-oasis belt 18m; savannah 11.5m; spice and tropical coasts 9.5m; dry plateaus/caravan highlands 5m; delta wetlands 3.037m. isolated when the creek rises | Regional fault lines: Lake dredging can damage fisheries and Merfolk communities, forestry revenues compete with Ent protection treaties, imported metal rises in price when western sea crossings fail, and mixed settlements require law rather than romantic stereotypes. ## Multi-species patchwork villages — new companion gazetteer The owner requested several folktale-like mixed communities where established smaller peoples and animal-featured peoples actually live and trade together rather than always forming single-species settlements. Eryndor Living Atlas VI — Patchwork Villages & Folktale Crossroads adds Candleburrow in Tharvorn, Saffronstep in Sahrad, Tanglelock in Orundel and Thornhollow and Shellbutton Reach in Vaelora. They have distinct food and water sources, laws, architecture, residents and cultural tensions. These names supplement rather than replace previously named cities and villages. Merfolk access requires genuine underwater/tidal facilities; Pixie/Brownie homes require small-scale protections. ## How small settlements actually work across all five continents Household cluster / steading: 5–40 residents, a well, rights to land or gathering, shared kin or chosen community, direct relationships with neighbors. Drought, illness or legal dispossession can end it. Hamlet: 40–250 residents, minor food surplus or specialist work, perhaps one mill, shrine, ferry, water pump or inn. Usually no professional market court. Residents walk to a village or seasonal market. Village: 250–2,500, multiple households and trades, grain store/communal hall, school or apprentices, water rights, annual fairs, taxes or a village council, a watch only when necessary. Large village / market town: 2,500–25,000, several specialized crafts, market squares, bridges and roads, magistrates, guild or clan associations, nearby dozens of hamlets; mobility and housing affect prices. Regional city: 25,000–300,000, stores, hospitals or healers, archives, many languages, urban food dependence, freight and banking. Great cities above 300k require extraordinary hinterlands and infrastructure. Species-specific scale: Pixie towns may occupy a single canopy; Goblin and Kobold cities can have extensive underground levels; Merfolk cities use three-dimensional ocean space; Centaur mobile camps relocate seasonally; Ent groves may have no compact urban population count. A “city” is a functional and political classification, not always a familiar street grid. ## Regional ecology — wildlife lives independently of adventures - Tharvorn: Elk, reindeer, sea birds, wolves, snow predators, fish, insect swarms in brief summers; preserve fish spawning and winter fodder. Bears are ordinary wildlife and separate from Bearfolk people. - Sahrad: Desert canids, lizards, antelopes, oasis fish, big cats, scavengers, raptors, livestock and river marshlife; lion species separate from Lionfolk people. - Orundel: Wetland birds, river fish, jungle insects and reptiles, large forest mammals, migratory steppe herds and local livestock; magical species to be named only when encountered and ecologically grounded. - Vaelora: Salmon, deer, boar, bears, wolves, wildcats, songbirds, marsh reptiles and deep-lake fauna; giant trees do not imply Ent sapience without examination. - Coasts everywhere: Storms, reefs, sea birds, marine predators, fish breeding, salt marshes and underwater Merfolk polities; piracy is a human or mixed social problem, not a monster species. ## Specific story-life consequences beyond Karak-Varn - Sahrad river sultanates can build floodgates, fight drought and protect river markets without Gloin ever visiting them. - Tharvorn chiefs can litigate hunting rights while fishermen face a poor spawning season. - Orundel river federations can collapse into tariffs or renegotiate a crucial treaty. - Vaelora forests can lose a logging concession, gain a preservation order or endure a lightning fire. - Merfolk sovereigns negotiate shipping corridors and reef damage; surface states cannot assume submerged waters are empty. - Urakai in Orundel do not automatically obey Avarra's reported warlord; similarly, independent Eldar settlements are not universally directed by Letharion. - Every adventuring lead is an opportunity, not a guaranteed secret about the First Throne, the lost magic art, Gloin's ancestry or the current eastern mine.
